findings.impact: The event flow throws a TypeError before it can fall back to the Daily integration, so bookings without a destination calendar fail.
findings.root_cause: The scalar destination-calendar access was changed to array destructuring without preserving the previous null-safe access.
findings.suggested_fix: Use optional chaining or an explicit presence check, for example `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.
findings.title: Avoid dereferencing a missing main destination calendar

findings.verifier_reason: Line 119 verbatim shows `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` accessed without optional chaining after destructuring from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`. When array is empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined, causing TypeError on `.integration` access.

findings.body: The lookup compares every external ID with `undefined` and produces an undefined `calendarId`, causing the Google update request to fail instead of updating the configured calendar.
findings.failure_mode: Updates of bookings without a stored external calendar ID cannot address the calendar containing the event.
findings.impact: The lookup compares every external ID with `undefined` and produces an undefined `calendarId`, causing the Google update request to fail instead of updating the configured calendar.
findings.root_cause: The old scalar fallback was converted into a search for an entry whose external ID equals the missing search value.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the first destination calendar’s external ID as the no-reference fallback, for example `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`, with an appropriate primary-calendar fallback.

findings.verifier_reason: Line 256 verbatim: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is falsy (else branch), searching for `cal.externalId === undefined` always returns undefined, making calendarId undefined and causing update to fail.

findings.body: The database booking retains only the first destination calendar, so later webhook, confirmation, reschedule, or retry flows reconstruct the event with only the main host and omit the other hosts’ calendars.
findings.failure_mode: Multi-host calendar routing works only during the in-memory operation and is lost across subsequent processes.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- Converts destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent to be an array.
- Patches and fixes so every sentence of code that was using evet.destinationCalendar can support the new type of array.
- The logic here is to fallback to normal behaviour has having one main destinationCalendar but also supports multiple so host can get invited correctly.

Fixes #7754 
## Loom 
Creating event and rescheduling:
https://www.loom.com/share/3cb3af513d274ed2bdfed44e48edddf6?sid=d81ce3de-2893-4a30-b085-ff67c31b7dfb

Canceling event:
https://www.loom.com/share/7ef505d4665e4d4982d2bb2d7b118085?sid=cd43c97c-aa86-4667-979f-f6492adf3365

## Requirement/Documentation

## Type of change

<!-- Please delete bullets that are not relevant. -->

- [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

- Are there environment variables that should be set? No
- What are the minimal test data to have? Setup a collective event using teampro and teamfree users. Add any app calendar to those accounts and add them as host for collective event.
- What is expected (happy path) to have (input and output)? Collective event with 2 host and every user with any calendar app installed should receive proper calendar events.
- Any other important info that could help to test that PR

## Mandatory Tasks

- [X] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use optional chaining or an explicit presence check, for example `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.
raw_findings.title: Avoid dereferencing a missing main destination calendar

raw_findings.body: No array entry matches the credential ID, so the event is inserted into Google’s `primary` calendar instead of the configured destination calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legacy or credential-less destination configuration silently routes new events to the wrong calendar.

raw_findings.root_cause: Calendar selection was changed from the configured destination external ID to a credential-ID-only lookup.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to the destination calendar’s external ID when no credential-ID match exists, while retaining credential matching for multi-host events.
raw_findings.title: Google event creation ignores configured calendars without credential IDs
raw_findings.trigger: Create a booking whose destination calendar has an `externalId` but no `credentialId`, such as a legacy destination-calendar record; `createAllCalendarEvents` invokes the Google service with the connected credential.

raw_findings.body: The lookup compares every external ID with `undefined` and produces an undefined `calendarId`, causing the Google update request to fail instead of updating the configured calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Updates of bookings without a stored external calendar ID cannot address the calendar containing the event.
raw_findings.impact: The lookup compares every external ID with `undefined` and produces an undefined `calendarId`, causing the Google update request to fail instead of updating the configured calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: The old scalar fallback was converted into a search for an entry whose external ID equals the missing search value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the first destination calendar’s external ID as the no-reference fallback, for example `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`, with an appropriate primary-calendar fallback.
raw_findings.title: Google updates lose the configured calendar when no reference external ID exists
raw_findings.trigger: Update a Google event when `externalCalendarId` is null or undefined but `event.destinationCalendar` contains the configured calendar.

raw_findings.body: The lookup returns undefined and the subsequent fallback selects `primary`; the actual event remains in its configured calendar because the delete is sent to the wrong calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cancellation can report success after deleting nothing from the calendar that contains the event.
raw_findings.impact: The lookup returns undefined and the subsequent fallback selects `primary`; the actual event remains in its configured calendar because the delete is sent to the wrong calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: Deletion uses the missing external ID as a search key instead of falling back to the event’s main destination calendar.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is absent, then use `primary` only when no destination exists.
raw_findings.title: Google deletion falls back to primary instead of the configured destination calendar
raw_findings.trigger: Cancel a Google event when the booking reference has no `externalCalendarId` and the event has a destination calendar configured.

raw_findings.body: The database booking retains only the first destination calendar, so later webhook, confirmation, reschedule, or retry flows reconstruct the event with only the main host and omit the other hosts’ calendars.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Multi-host calendar routing works only during the in-memory operation and is lost across subsequent processes.
raw_findings.impact: The database booking retains only the first destination calendar, so later webhook, confirmation, reschedule, or retry flows reconstruct the event with only the main host and omit the other hosts’ calendars.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new array is reduced to index zero when writing the existing singular `Booking.destinationCalendar` relation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Persist all destination-calendar associations in a relation that supports multiple records, or persist the complete destination list in the booking data and load it in every event reconstruction path.
raw_findings.title: Only the first destination calendar is persisted for multi-host bookings
raw_findings.trigger: Create a collective booking whose event contains destination calendars for multiple hosts, especially when calendar creation is deferred until payment confirmation or a later booking operation reloads the booking.

raw_findings.body: The replacement booking references lose the calendar external ID (and the adjacent credential ID), so later updates and cancellations cannot reliably target the calendar where the event was created.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A successful location update corrupts the persisted reference needed for future calendar operations.
raw_findings.impact: The replacement booking references lose the calendar external ID (and the adjacent credential ID), so later updates and cancellations cannot reliably target the calendar where the event was created.
raw_findings.root_cause: Updated reference metadata is sourced from fields that update results do not provide instead of from the existing calendar reference.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the routing metadata from the existing reference or destination entry, or make `CalendarManager.updateEvent` return the external and credential IDs before constructing `referencesToCreate`.
raw_findings.title: Location updates drop calendar routing metadata from replacement references
raw_findings.trigger: Edit the location of an existing booking and persist the `referencesToCreate` returned by `updateLocation`; `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not populate `externalId` or `credentialId` on its result.

raw_findings.body: The update path processes all new references, but the later cleanup still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so only the first old calendar event is deleted and the remaining host events become stale.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Rescheduling leaves duplicate events on secondary host calendars.
raw_findings.impact: The update path processes all new references, but the later cleanup still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so only the first old calendar event is deleted and the remaining host events become stale.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch expands reference processing to arrays without expanding the old-event cleanup from a single reference to all references.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Filter all old calendar references and delete each one using its own credential and external calendar ID.
raw_findings.title: Rescheduling deletes only one of multiple old calendar events
raw_findings.trigger: Reschedule or merge a booking with multiple calendar references by supplying `newBookingId`.

raw_findings.body: Every Lark creation uses the first destination calendar ID, so secondary host events are duplicated into the main host calendar or fail when the second account cannot access that calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Multi-host Lark event creation does not follow the destination-to-credential mapping.
raw_findings.impact: Every Lark creation uses the first destination calendar ID, so secondary host events are duplicated into the main host calendar or fail when the second account cannot access that calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: The service adapts the array by selecting only its first element even though the caller now iterates over every destination.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the selected destination or credential ID into the Lark service and select the matching destination instead of always destructuring index zero.
raw_findings.title: Lark creation always targets the first destination calendar
raw_findings.trigger: Create a collective event with two Lark destination calendars; `EventManager` invokes creation once for each destination and credential.

raw_findings.body: The Office 365 request URL is built with the first host’s calendar ID for every credential, so secondary host events are written to the wrong calendar or rejected by Microsoft Graph.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Office 365 multi-host creation routes all events to the main destination.
raw_findings.impact: The Office 365 request URL is built with the first host’s calendar ID for every credential, so secondary host events are written to the wrong calendar or rejected by Microsoft Graph.
raw_findings.root_cause: The service ignores the per-destination iteration introduced by the patch and always uses array element zero.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Propagate the selected destination or credential ID to the service and select the matching Office 365 calendar for each creation.
raw_findings.title: Office 365 creation always targets the first destination calendar
raw_findings.trigger: Create a collective event with multiple Office 365 destination calendars; `EventManager` calls the service for each destination credential.

raw_findings.body: Each invocation filters the available calendars against the first destination external ID, so secondary destinations receive no event or the wrong calendar object is selected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inherited calendar integrations silently omit secondary host events.
raw_findings.impact: Each invocation filters the available calendars against the first destination external ID, so secondary destinations receive no event or the wrong calendar object is selected.
raw_findings.root_cause: The scalar destination filter was converted to an array but retained first-element semantics while the caller began processing multiple destinations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the selected destination or credential into the base service and filter against that destination; do not use a global first-array-element fallback for each invocation.
raw_findings.title: Inherited iCalendar services still filter to only the first destination
raw_findings.trigger: Create a multi-host event through a calendar integration inheriting `BaseCalendarService`, where `EventManager` invokes creation for more than one destination.

raw_findings.body: The recurring cleanup iterates only the organizer’s loaded credentials, so future instances on the fetched host credential are not deleted.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cancellation appears to complete while recurring events remain on a team host’s calendar.
raw_findings.impact: The recurring cleanup iterates only the organizer’s loaded credentials, so future instances on the fetched host credential are not deleted.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new fallback resolves a missing reference credential for the single-event branch, but the recurring branch still derives its deletion credentials exclusively from the organizer’s credential list.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Include the resolved `calendarCredential` in the recurring deletion set or delete each updated booking using its individual calendar reference and credential.

raw_findings.trigger: Cancel a recurring collective booking when a calendar reference belongs to a host credential that is absent from `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and was loaded through the new database fallback.

validated_findings.root_cause: Calendar selection was changed from the configured destination external ID to a credential-ID-only lookup.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to the destination calendar’s external ID when no credential-ID match exists, while retaining credential matching for multi-host events.
validated_findings.title: Google event creation ignores configured calendars without credential IDs
validated_findings.trigger: Create a booking whose destination calendar has an `externalId` but no `credentialId`, such as a legacy destination-calendar record; `createAllCalendarEvents` invokes the Google service with the connected credential.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at line 147-149 shows credential-ID lookup with fallback to 'primary' at line 154. Legacy records without credentialId would still work via the fallback. The claim that events go to wrong calendar is speculative - the fallback behavior is intentional.

validated_findings.body: The lookup compares every external ID with `undefined` and produces an undefined `calendarId`, causing the Google update request to fail instead of updating the configured calendar.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Updates of bookings without a stored external calendar ID cannot address the calendar containing the event.
validated_findings.impact: The lookup compares every external ID with `undefined` and produces an undefined `calendarId`, causing the Google update request to fail instead of updating the configured calendar.
validated_findings.root_cause: The old scalar fallback was converted into a search for an entry whose external ID equals the missing search value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use the first destination calendar’s external ID as the no-reference fallback, for example `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`, with an appropriate primary-calendar fallback.
validated_findings.title: Google updates lose the configured calendar when no reference external ID exists
validated_findings.trigger: Update a Google event when `externalCalendarId` is null or undefined but `event.destinationCalendar` contains the configured calendar.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 256 verbatim: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is falsy (else branch), searching for `cal.externalId === undefined` always returns undefined, making calendarId undefined and causing update to fail.

validated_findings.body: The lookup returns undefined and the subsequent fallback selects `primary`; the actual event remains in its configured calendar because the delete is sent to the wrong calendar.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Cancellation can report success after deleting nothing from the calendar that contains the event.
validated_findings.impact: The lookup returns undefined and the subsequent fallback selects `primary`; the actual event remains in its configured calendar because the delete is sent to the wrong calendar.
validated_findings.root_cause: Deletion uses the missing external ID as a search key instead of falling back to the event’s main destination calendar.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is absent, then use `primary` only when no destination exists.
validated_findings.title: Google deletion falls back to primary instead of the configured destination calendar
validated_findings.trigger: Cancel a Google event when the booking reference has no `externalCalendarId` and the event has a destination calendar configured.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 317 has identical bug pattern to candidate 2: searching for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` when externalCalendarId is falsy. Same root cause, same fix needed, but different method (deleteEvent vs updateEvent).

validated_findings.body: The database booking retains only the first destination calendar, so later webhook, confirmation, reschedule, or retry flows reconstruct the event with only the main host and omit the other hosts’ calendars.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Multi-host calendar routing works only during the in-memory operation and is lost across subsequent processes.
validated_findings.impact: The database booking retains only the first destination calendar, so later webhook, confirmation, reschedule, or retry flows reconstruct the event with only the main host and omit the other hosts’ calendars.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new array is reduced to index zero when writing the existing singular `Booking.destinationCalendar` relation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Persist all destination-calendar associations in a relation that supports multiple records, or persist the complete destination list in the booking data and load it in every event reconstruction path.
validated_findings.title: Only the first destination calendar is persisted for multi-host bookings
validated_findings.trigger: Create a collective booking whose event contains destination calendars for multiple hosts, especially when calendar creation is deferred until payment confirmation or a later booking operation reloads the booking.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 1877 verbatim shows `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` - only first calendar persisted. Schema shows Booking has single destinationCalendarId relation. Multi-host calendars beyond index 0 are lost in DB.

validated_findings.body: The replacement booking references lose the calendar external ID (and the adjacent credential ID), so later updates and cancellations cannot reliably target the calendar where the event was created.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A successful location update corrupts the persisted reference needed for future calendar operations.
validated_findings.impact: The replacement booking references lose the calendar external ID (and the adjacent credential ID), so later updates and cancellations cannot reliably target the calendar where the event was created.
validated_findings.root_cause: Updated reference metadata is sourced from fields that update results do not provide instead of from the existing calendar reference.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the routing metadata from the existing reference or destination entry, or make `CalendarManager.updateEvent` return the external and credential IDs before constructing `referencesToCreate`.
validated_findings.title: Location updates drop calendar routing metadata from replacement references
validated_findings.trigger: Edit the location of an existing booking and persist the `referencesToCreate` returned by `updateLocation`; `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not populate `externalId` or `credentialId` on its result.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 208 shows `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`. The EventResult type shows externalId is optional. CalendarManager.updateEvent at line 272-322 doesn't populate externalId in its return, so result.externalId is undefined, losing routing metadata.

validated_findings.body: The update path processes all new references, but the later cleanup still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so only the first old calendar event is deleted and the remaining host events become stale.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Rescheduling leaves duplicate events on secondary host calendars.
validated_findings.impact: The update path processes all new references, but the later cleanup still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so only the first old calendar event is deleted and the remaining host events become stale.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch expands reference processing to arrays without expanding the old-event cleanup from a single reference to all references.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Filter all old calendar references and delete each one using its own credential and external calendar ID.
validated_findings.title: Rescheduling deletes only one of multiple old calendar events
validated_findings.trigger: Reschedule or merge a booking with multiple calendar references by supplying `newBookingId`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 495-497 show calendarReference changed to filter (array), but line 554 still uses `booking.references.find(...)` returning single reference. Only first old calendar event deleted when merging bookings with multiple references.

validated_findings.body: Every Lark creation uses the first destination calendar ID, so secondary host events are duplicated into the main host calendar or fail when the second account cannot access that calendar.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Multi-host Lark event creation does not follow the destination-to-credential mapping.
validated_findings.impact: Every Lark creation uses the first destination calendar ID, so secondary host events are duplicated into the main host calendar or fail when the second account cannot access that calendar.
validated_findings.root_cause: The service adapts the array by selecting only its first element even though the caller now iterates over every destination.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the selected destination or credential ID into the Lark service and select the matching destination instead of always destructuring index zero.
validated_findings.title: Lark creation always targets the first destination calendar
validated_findings.trigger: Create a collective event with two Lark destination calendars; `EventManager` invokes creation once for each destination and credential.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 128 verbatim: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`. Lark always uses first destination regardless of which credential is calling. EventManager iterates destinations but Lark ignores the iteration context.

validated_findings.body: The Office 365 request URL is built with the first host’s calendar ID for every credential, so secondary host events are written to the wrong calendar or rejected by Microsoft Graph.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Office 365 multi-host creation routes all events to the main destination.
validated_findings.impact: The Office 365 request URL is built with the first host’s calendar ID for every credential, so secondary host events are written to the wrong calendar or rejected by Microsoft Graph.
validated_findings.root_cause: The service ignores the per-destination iteration introduced by the patch and always uses array element zero.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Propagate the selected destination or credential ID to the service and select the matching Office 365 calendar for each creation.
validated_findings.title: Office 365 creation always targets the first destination calendar
validated_findings.trigger: Create a collective event with multiple Office 365 destination calendars; `EventManager` calls the service for each destination credential.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 73 shows identical pattern to candidate 7: Office365 destructures first element only. Same root cause - service ignores per-destination iteration from EventManager. Same fix pattern needed.

validated_findings.body: Each invocation filters the available calendars against the first destination external ID, so secondary destinations receive no event or the wrong calendar object is selected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inherited calendar integrations silently omit secondary host events.
validated_findings.impact: Each invocation filters the available calendars against the first destination external ID, so secondary destinations receive no event or the wrong calendar object is selected.
validated_findings.root_cause: The scalar destination filter was converted to an array but retained first-element semantics while the caller began processing multiple destinations.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the selected destination or credential into the base service and filter against that destination; do not use a global first-array-element fallback for each invocation.
validated_findings.title: Inherited iCalendar services still filter to only the first destination
validated_findings.trigger: Create a multi-host event through a calendar integration inheriting `BaseCalendarService`, where `EventManager` invokes creation for more than one destination.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 156-163 show same pattern as candidates 7,8: BaseCalendarService filters to mainHostDestinationCalendar[0] only. Same root cause of ignoring multi-host iteration.

validated_findings.body: The recurring cleanup iterates only the organizer’s loaded credentials, so future instances on the fetched host credential are not deleted.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Cancellation appears to complete while recurring events remain on a team host’s calendar.
validated_findings.impact: The recurring cleanup iterates only the organizer’s loaded credentials, so future instances on the fetched host credential are not deleted.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new fallback resolves a missing reference credential for the single-event branch, but the recurring branch still derives its deletion credentials exclusively from the organizer’s credential list.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Include the resolved `calendarCredential` in the recurring deletion set or delete each updated booking using its individual calendar reference and credential.
validated_findings.title: Recurring cancellation misses a credential loaded from the database
validated_findings.trigger: Cancel a recurring collective booking when a calendar reference belongs to a host credential that is absent from `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and was loaded through the new database fallback.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 449 shows recurring deletion uses `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` exclusively. The new DB fallback at lines 431-439 loads calendarCredential but it's not added to the credentials iterated at line 449-451 for recurring events.
